- **Payment cost omitted from headline math:** Main's "Fulfil 600 + commission 150 → 750 contribution" excludes any payment-processing fee. Appendix shows real processing cost is 3% on the full 11500 = 345, not the ~150 implied elsewhere. If applied per-campaign, the 750 contribution figure could shrink materially — add a one-line caveat that 750 excludes payment processing, addressed only in the appendix payback sensitivity.

- **Rate inconsistency between illustrations:** Headline example (10000 reward / 1500 fee) establishes a 15% platform fee. But 150 commission on 600 fulfil implies 25% (150/600), not 15%. Either these are unrelated illustrative scales (say so explicitly) or the numbers need reconciling — as written it reads as one consistent rate applied twice, which it isn't.

- **"Commission" double-count risk:** Appendix's commission 3000 (=150 Ă— 20 campaigns) is subtracted from GP as a cost in the operating calc. Confirm this isn't already embedded in the 30000 revenue line — if the 15% fee is both revenue-in and a deducted cost, operating income is understated/overstated depending on direction. This needs an explicit accounting-treatment note, not just "NOT CAC."

- **"1500" reused for two different concepts:** Main uses 1500 as the platform's fee on a 10000 campaign (margin). Appendix uses 1500 as average total revenue per campaign (30000/20, gross throughput including pass-through rewards). These are very different numbers conceptually; label them distinctly to avoid a reader conflating fee take-rate with gross volume.

- **Main headline vs. appendix bottom line not cross-referenced:** Main's "750 contribution before fixed/CAC" and appendix's "-2000 operating after fixed" are arithmetically consistent (20Ă—750 = 15000; minus 17000 total fixed = -2000), but main never states this scenario nets negative before new-brand CAC. A reader who only sees the main slide could walk away thinking unit economics are net-positive; add one summary line linking the two.

- **GP%/revenue figures contingent on unresolved accounting treatment:** 30000 revenue and 53.33% GP% assume gross (not net) service-fee revenue recognition, which the draft itself marks unresolved. If switched to net, both headline numbers change. This dependency should sit next to the GP% figure, not only in a footnote, since it's currently presented as if settled.
